name: Height, body mass, and BMI
definition: Anthropometric body dimensions (Body Mass Index in kg/m^2 and mid-upper arm circumference in cm) measured by trained examiners following standardized CDC health examination protocols.
comparison_note: Direct stadiometer and digital scale measurements are clinic physical determinations and must not be pooled with self-reported survey height and weight, which exhibit systematic under-reporting of body weight and over-reporting of height.
methodological_warning: Wrist and arm circumference directly govern sensor optical coupling and motion artifact vulnerability. Subcutaneous adipose tissue (BMI) alters optical photon path lengths.

sources.title: NHANES 2015-2018, mid-upper arm circumference (cm)

population.description: Civilian, non-institutionalised US residents aged 18 and over examined in the mobile examination centre, two survey cycles combined (2015-2016 and 2017-2018).
population.exclusions: Adults examined without upper arm circumference determinations or with physical arm casts/amputations are left out.

measurement.method: Mid-upper arm circumference measured in centimeters at the midpoint between the acromion and olecranon process of the right arm.
measurement.protocol: Participant stands erect with right arm bent 90 degrees to locate midpoint, then arm relaxes freely while examiner measures circumference without compressing subcutaneous skin tissue.

analysis: Estimates use the examination sampling weights (WTMEC2YR), halved for the two combined cycles.
Percentiles are calculated from the survey-weighted empirical distribution.
95% confidence intervals are derived from 500 Rao-Wu bootstrap resamples of primary sampling units within strata.
Subgroups with fewer than 50 examined individuals are suppressed.
use_for: Sizing wearable armbands, blood pressure cuffs, and upper-arm sensor straps.
Establishing mechanical fit bounds across diverse adult arm circumferences.
do_not_use_for: A direct proxy for wrist circumference: wrist circumference is smaller and has a higher bone-to-soft-tissue ratio than mid-upper arm.
Pediatric cuff sizing: restricted to adults aged 18 and over.
caveats: **Upper arm, not wrist.** Upper arm circumference is 10-15 cm larger than wrist circumference; do not use as wrist strap length without offset calibration.
**Age 80 and over is top-coded** at 80 years in accordance with NCHS participant disclosure rules.

citation.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey Data, 2015-2018. Hyattsville, MD: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
citation.license: NCHS public-use data file. Users must use data for statistical reporting and analysis only.

sources.verification: The overall survey-weighted arm circumference mean of 33.2 cm aligns with published CDC anthropometric reference data.

sources.title: NHANES 2015-2018, body mass index (BMI)

population.description: Civilian, non-institutionalised US residents aged 18 and over examined in the mobile examination centre, two survey cycles combined (2015-2016 and 2017-2018).
population.exclusions: None for health conditions or pregnancy. Adults examined without standing height or weight determinations are left out.

measurement.method: Body Mass Index calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared (kg/m^2).
measurement.device: Mettler Toledo digital scale and calibrated stadiometer.
measurement.protocol: Measured in disposable examination gown and foam slippers following standardized anthropometric procedures.

analysis: Estimates use the examination sampling weights (WTMEC2YR), halved for the two combined cycles.
Percentiles are calculated from the survey-weighted empirical distribution.
95% confidence intervals are derived from 500 Rao-Wu bootstrap resamples of primary sampling units within strata.
Subgroups with fewer than 50 examined individuals are suppressed.
use_for: Sizing wearable validation cohorts to ensure representative distribution across normal, overweight, and class I-III obesity tiers.
Quantifying between-subject variation in body size across age, sex, and race/ethnicity.
do_not_use_for: A direct measure of body fat percentage or body composition: BMI does not differentiate lean mass from adipose tissue.
Athletic elite cohorts: high muscle mass athletes are misclassified into overweight or obese brackets.
caveats: **Heavy right tail.** BMI exhibits strong positive skewness; mean is consistently higher than median.
**Age 80 and over is top-coded** at 80 years in accordance with NCHS participant disclosure rules.

citation.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey Data, 2015-2018. Hyattsville, MD: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
citation.license: NCHS public-use data file. Users must use data for statistical reporting and analysis only.

sources.verification: The overall survey-weighted BMI mean of 29.7 kg/m^2 aligns with published CDC NCHS reference tables for the 2015-2018 survey cycles.
